feedback_given: Your diagnosis of Pulmonary Embolism is correct and demonstrates a good understanding of the patient's presenting symptoms.
To further confirm this diagnosis, a key investigation that would have been valuable is the D-dimer test, as it can help assess the likelihood of a thromboembolic event.
Additionally, performing a Lower Limb exam could have provided important information on potential deep vein thrombosis, a common cause of pulmonary embolism.
A 12-lead ECG would also have been useful to rule out other cardiac causes of the patient's symptoms.
